Republic 01" the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Www.dilg.gov.ph SERVICE DILG Legal Opinion No. 24, S. 2013 05 RAMONITA CENTINO centram@yahoo.com Dear Ms. Centino: This pertains to your email posing a query which we hereby quote in toto, viz: "DOES THE RETROACTIVE EFFECT OF APPROPRIATION ORDINANCE ENABLE LOCAL GOVERNMENT TO ENTER INTO CONTIeACT'S PRIOR TO THE APPROVAL OF THEIR BUDGET?" Perhaps, you are referring to the reenactment of appropriation ordinance of the preceding year in case the sanggunian concerned failed to enact the appropriation ordinance within ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year. Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) is unequivocal in respect to what items of the appropriations shall be deemed reenacted, thus: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However. only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions. statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. (emphasis ours)

Based on the aforequoted provision, only the annual appropriations for contractual obligations for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted if the sanggunian fails to enact the appropriation ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year. Therefore, in such cases, only existing contracts entered into by local government units from their preceding year's appropriation ordinance are deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. Accordingly, a local government unit can enter into contracts before its current year's appropriation ordinance has been passed by the sanggunian; provided that funds for such new contracts may not be disbursed yet until the appropriation ordinance for the current year has been enacted, in conformity with Section 323 of the LGC. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, J SUS . o Dire tor II Ls:2
